summary:
**Visual similarity: 9.0/10.** The supplied native renders meet the requested visual threshold, with minor remaining differences.

| Category | Score |
|---|---:|
| Hierarchy | 9.1 |
| Proportions | 8.8 |
| Surfaces | 9.2 |
| Typography | 9.0 |
| Thumbnails and queue | 9.0 |
| Controls and discovery | 9.1 |
| Responsive usability | 9.0 |

I inspected the web reference and actual desktop, compact, short, Stage, Focus, wide, and desktop belowfold renders. The charcoal cards, thumbnail queue, selected-row treatment, white transport controls, shuffle panel, and suggestions surface clearly reproduce the reference’s visual language.

The short-window refinement resolves the previous major proportion issue: media now measures approximately **619×348** at compact size, **690×388** at short desktop size, and **868×488** in Stage. Transport remains visible, and the measured video boxes retain 16:9. The measurement artifact now correctly separates initial and scrolled coordinates.

Remaining refinements are minor:

- At 1280×860, the 722-point video remains inset within an 876-point deck, giving broader shoulders than the reference’s nearly full-width media.
- Native queue rows and chrome feel slightly more spacious; the reference has a denser listening-console appearance.
- The belowfold shortcuts button spans its container, while the reference uses a smaller centered button within that surface.

I found no remaining visual blocker requiring another implementation round to reach 9/10. Compact Queue/Shuffle affordances, explicit playback actions, and visible “Stop & close” remain present.

This is **visual signoff only** from source, PNGs, and exported geometry. I did not rerun tests or interactively verify controls. Static artwork and synthetic paused callbacks do not establish live YouTube, audio, account, OS-control, or policy acceptance; those gates remain open and did not reduce the visual score. No files changed.
